subtype: Approach: ask for details and independent information [Thinking]
passage:
Tuesday. Swati took me to the wellness circle again, and this time I made myself ask. Where does the monthly contribution go? Who runs it? Why can't members see accounts? The leader smiled and said, "Trust is part of the journey." That is not an answer. Tonight I searched the group's name with the word "complaints" and found two news reports and a post by an ex-member who was told to cut off her sister. I showed Swati. Swati said they were just bitter people. Maybe. But a group that goes cold when you ask where the money goes doesn't feel healthy to me. I'm not going on Thursday. Not deciding forever, only this week.

Dilnaz

qa.q: Which questions did Dilnaz ask the leader?
qa.a: Dilnaz asked where the monthly contribution goes, who runs the circle and why members can't see accounts.

qa.q: What did Dilnaz think of the leader's reply?
qa.a: Dilnaz felt uneasy and unsatisfied, because "Trust is part of the journey" did not answer anything.

qa.q: What else could Dilnaz do to understand the group, and why?
qa.a: Dilnaz could talk it over with a family member or a college counsellor and read more accounts from former members, because outside experience helps check the group's own story.

qa.q: How might Swati feel about Dilnaz's decision not to go?
qa.a: Swati might feel defensive and hurt, having brought Dilnaz along and believing the circle has been good for others.

grounding: Illustrates asking where funds go, who leads and what former members say, and looking up independent information about a group.
